tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

160	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
161	
162	顶层文件是"名词表"，子包则是按**生命周期阶段**划分的"车间"：提示词怎么写（prompts）、输入要不要丢弃（filter）、页面怎么变成图片（data）、模型怎么训练（train）、效果怎么评（bench）、训练数据怎么造（synth）、结果怎么人工抽查（viewer）。理解子包 = 理解 olmOCR 这个项目的业务闭环：
163	
164	```text
165	真实 PDF ──(pipeline 主流水线，用 prompts/data/filter)──> Markdown/Dolma
166	                                        │
167	     synth 合成数据 + data 里的 GPT-4o silver 数据
168	                                        │
169	                                        ▼
170	                            train（SFT + GRPO，奖励来自 bench）
171	                                        │
172	                                        ▼
173	                            bench 评测 ──> viewer 人工抽查
174	```

233	**练习 2**：`data/renderpdf.py` 的 `render_pdf_to_base64png` 被哪些子包引用？这说明了什么？
234	
235	> **答案**：被 `pipeline.py`（L36）、`bench/`（convert.py、runners/、miners/、report.py 等十余处）、`synth/mine_html_templates.py`、`viewer/dolmaviewer.py`、`data/` 内部脚本、`train/grpo_train.py` 引用——它是全仓库被复用最广的函数之一，"把一页 PDF 渲染成模型/评测都能吃的图片"是所有子包的共同底座。
236	
237	**练习 3**：想给 OCR 结果做人工质量抽查，应该用哪个子包？它依赖哪两个模块获取原始 PDF 和页面图片？
238	
239	> **答案**：`viewer/`（`dolmaviewer.py`）。它 import 了 [olmocr/viewer/dolmaviewer.py:16-17](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/viewer/dolmaviewer.py#L16-L17)：`data.renderpdf.render_pdf_to_base64webp`（渲染页面）和 `s3_utils`（`get_s3_bytes`/`parse_s3_path` 取原始 PDF，支持 tarball 双冒号路径）。
240	
241	### 4.3 模块间依赖草图：谁 import 谁
242	
243	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
244	
245	架构不是画出来的，是 **import 出来的**。把每个文件里的 `from olmocr.X import ...` 收集起来，就得到一张真实的依赖图。olmocr 的依赖图呈清晰的"沙漏形"：
246	
247	- **上层（消费端）**：`pipeline.py`（推理）与 `train/`（训练）——两个各自完整的程序；
248	- **中层（领域层）**：`prompts/`、`data/`、`filter/`、`bench/`——推理和训练都要用的共享能力；
249	- **底座（基础设施）**：`s3_utils.py`、`work_queue.py`、`metrics.py`、`image_utils.py` 等工具文件。
250	
251	关键结论（也是本讲规格要求的学习目标）：**`pipeline`、`work_queue`、`train`、`bench` 四者中，`pipeline` 和 `train` 是平级的两个入口；`work_queue` 只服务于 `pipeline`（及其多机扩展）；`bench` 是 `train`（GRPO 奖励）与 `synth`（质检）共同依赖的下游裁判。**
252	
253	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
254	
255	推导依赖草图的伪代码：
256	
257	```text
258	对 olmocr/ 下每个 .py 文件 F：
259	    抽取 F 中所有 "from olmocr.X..." 与 "import olmocr.X..." 行
260	    对每个 X 画边 F → X
261	忽略指向自身的边，得到边集 E
262	
263	观察 E：
264	    1. 入度最高的节点 = 公共底座（预期：data.renderpdf、s3_utils、prompts）
265	    2. 出度最高的节点 = 总装配厂（预期：pipeline.py）
266	    3. 若出现环 = 值得警惕的设计（预期：没有）
267	```
268	
269	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
270	
271	四条最有代表性的"依赖边"，每条都给出了铁证：
272	
273	**边 1：pipeline → 几乎全世界。** [olmocr/pipeline.py:32-52](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L32-L52) 的 import 块一口气引了 `check`、`data.renderpdf`、`filter.filter`、`image_utils`、`metrics`、`prompts`、`prompts.anchor`、`s3_utils`、`train.front_matter`、`version`、`work_queue` 共 11 个内部模块——它是唯一"认识所有车间"的总装配厂：
274	
275	```python
276	from olmocr.check import (check_poppler_version, check_torch_gpu_available)
277	from olmocr.data.renderpdf import render_pdf_to_base64png
278	from olmocr.filter.filter import Language, PdfFilter
279	from olmocr.image_utils import convert_image_to_pdf_bytes, is_jpeg, is_png
280	from olmocr.metrics import MetricsKeeper, WorkerTracker
281	from olmocr.prompts import PageResponse, build_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_prompt
282	from olmocr.prompts.anchor import get_anchor_text
283	from olmocr.s3_utils import (download_directory, download_zstd_csv, ...)
284	from olmocr.train.front_matter import FrontMatterParser
285	from olmocr.version import VERSION
286	from olmocr.work_queue import LocalBackend, S3Backend, WorkQueue
287	```
288	
289	**边 2：work_queue → s3_utils。** [olmocr/work_queue.py:16-21](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/work_queue.py#L16-L21) 只引了 4 个 S3 函数——队列抽象站在存储工具之上，且**不依赖** pipeline/train/bench 任何一个。
290	
291	**边 3：train → bench（olmOCR-2 的灵魂边）。** [olmocr/train/grpo_train.py:34-38](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/train/grpo_train.py#L34-L38)：
292	
293	```python
294	from olmocr.bench.table_parsing import parse_html_tables
295	from olmocr.bench.tests import load_single_test
296	from olmocr.data.renderpdf import render_pdf_to_base64png
297	from olmocr.prompts import PageResponse, build_no_anchoring_v4_yaml_prompt
298	from olmocr.train.front_matter import FrontMatterParser
299	```
300	
301	训练代码 import 评测代码，正是"把 olmOCR-Bench 单元测试当作 GRPO 奖励函数"这一核心创新在依赖图上的投影（u6-l3 精读）。
302	
303	**边 4：synth → bench + data + filter；viewer → data + s3_utils。** [olmocr/synth/mine_html_templates.py:25-50](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/synth/mine_html_templates.py#L25-L50) 同时引 `bench.tests`（质检）、`data.renderpdf`（渲染）、`filter.filter`（筛选）；[olmocr/viewer/dolmaviewer.py:16-17](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/viewer/dolmaviewer.py#L16-L17) 只引 `data.renderpdf` 与 `s3_utils`。
304	
305	把这些边汇总成草图（箭头 = "import"）：
306	
307	```text
308	pipeline.py ──→ work_queue ──→ s3_utils ←── viewer
309	     │                            ↑
310	     ├──→ train.front_matter      │
311	     ├──→ prompts ←───────────────┼──── train/（grpo_train、dataloader）
312	     ├──→ data.renderpdf ←────────┼──────── bench/、synth/、viewer
313	     ├──→ filter.filter ←─────────┼──────── bench/miners、synth、data
314	     ├──→ metrics、check、image_utils、version
315	     │
316	     │            train/grpo_train ──→ bench.tests   ★ 灵魂边
317	     └──────────── bench/tests ──→ repeatdetect
318	```
319	
320	反方向验证：`bench/runners/run_olmocr_pipeline.py` 的 `from olmocr.pipeline import ...` 是评测框架调被测对象，属于"工具脚本调程序"，不改变"pipeline 平时不认识 bench"的结论（pipeline.py 的 import 块里确实没有 `olmocr.bench`）。
321	
322	#### 4.3.4 代码实践（源码阅读型：用 grep 亲手量出依赖图）
323	
324	1. **实践目标**：自动生成全仓库的 `olmocr` 内部依赖边清单，验证 4.3.3 的草图。
325	2. **操作步骤**：在仓库根目录执行：
326	
327	   ```bash
328	   grep -rn "^from olmocr\.\|^import olmocr\." olmocr/ --include="*.py" \
329	     | sed 's/:from olmocr\.\([a-z_.]*\).*/ -> olmocr.\1/' > /tmp/olmocr_deps.txt
330	   sort /tmp/olmocr_deps.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -40
331	   ```
332	
333	   第一条命令把每处内部 import 变成 `文件 -> 模块` 的边；第二条统计每条边出现的次数并按频次排序。
334	
335	3. **需要观察的现象**：输出里 `-> olmocr.data.renderpdf` 的行会霸榜（十几个文件引它）；`olmocr/pipeline.py -> ...` 只有 1 行却引了 11 个模块；几乎看不到指向 `olmocr.pipeline` 的边（只有 `bench/runners/run_olmocr_pipeline.py` 一处）。
336	4. **预期结果**：你得到的频次榜应当与"沙漏形"结论一致——`data.renderpdf`、`s3_utils`、`prompts`、`filter.filter` 是被引最多的底座。grep/sed 只做文本处理，任何环境都能跑；本讲义环境未执行此命令，输出细节**待本地验证**。
337	
338	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
339	
340	**练习 1**：`work_queue.py` 有没有 import `pipeline.py`？这个事实有什么工程意义？
341	
342	> **答案**：没有——`work_queue.py` 只 import `olmocr.s3_utils`（L16-21）。意义：队列模块可以脱离整条流水线被单独测试、单独复用（u3-l1 的实践就会单独实例化 `LocalBackend` + `WorkQueue`），依赖单向是模块可独立测试的前提。
343	
344	**练习 2**：`pipeline.py` 的 import 块里有 `from olmocr.train.front_matter import FrontMatterParser`，却不曾 import `olmocr.bench`。结合 u1-l1 讲过的"olmOCR-2 = 合成数据 + GRPO"，说说为什么这个不对称是合理的？
345	
346	> **答案**：推理流水线只需要"解析模型输出的 front matter"，这段逻辑与训练数据解析同源，所以复用 `train/front_matter.py`；而评测（bench）属于训练/研究侧的下游环节——推理时不需要知道自己会被谁打分。反过来 `train/grpo_train.py` 必须引用 `bench.tests`，因为奖励就是测试通过率。不对称恰恰反映了"推理轻、训练重"的职责切分。
347	
348	**练习 3**：如果让你新增一个"把结果上传到某内部系统"的功能，按现有依赖方向，它应该放哪里？为什么？
349	
350	> **答案**：参考 `viewer/` 的做法——做成一个只依赖 `s3_utils`/`data.renderpdf` 等底座的新子包或脚本，让 pipeline 的落盘产物（Dolma JSONL / Markdown）作为它的输入，而不是往 `pipeline.py` 里加 import。保持 pipeline 不认识它，才能不加重这个已经 1500+ 行的总装配厂。
351	
352	## 5. 综合实践
353	
354	**任务：制作你自己的《olmocr 模块地图卡片》**（纯源码阅读，不需要 GPU，不需要 pip 安装任何新东西）。
355	
356	1. **目标**：产出一份一页纸的地图，包含三个区块，以后每读一篇讲义就回来在地图上"点亮"一个模块。
357	2. **步骤**：
358	   - **区块 A（名词表）**：完成 4.1.4 的 9 行顶层文件职责表。
359	   - **区块 B（车间表）**：为 7 个子包各写一行"职责 + 对外接口（看 `__init__.py` 或最核心的一个类/函数）+ 服务的生命周期阶段（推理时/训练前/训练后）"。
360	   - **区块 C（依赖边）**：运行 4.3.4 的 grep 管线，把 `uniq -c` 频次前 10 的依赖边抄进地图，并标出唯一一条 `train → bench` 边。
361	   - 最后在地图底部写一行"验证日期 + HEAD 提交号"（当前为 `f7cfe4c`），因为行号会随版本漂移。
362	3. **自查标准**：只看你的地图、不看讲义，能回答出以下三问即算通过——
363	   - `olmocr` 命令的入口链条是什么？（cli_main → main）
364	   - 被最多模块复用的渲染函数在哪？（`data/renderpdf.py` 的 `render_pdf_to_base64png`）
365	   - 为什么训练代码要 import 评测代码？（GRPO 奖励 = bench 单测通过率）
366	
367	## 6. 本讲小结
368	
369	- `olmocr/` 根目录 9 个 `.py` 是"名词表"：`pipeline.py` 是总装配厂与 CLI 入口，`work_queue.py` 提供可断点续跑的队列抽象（`Backend` + 本地/S3 双实现），其余是 metrics/s3/image/check/version 等工具与 `datatypes.py` 这个已无人引用的历史遗留。
370	- 七个子包按生命周期分工：`prompts`（提示词与输出契约）、`filter`（输入筛选）、`data`（渲染与数据准备）、`train`（SFT/GRPO）、`bench`（单元测试式评测）、`synth`（合成数据）、`viewer`（人工抽查）。

# u1-l4 仓库结构与模块地图

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 `olmocr/` 包下每个顶层 `.py` 文件（`pipeline.py`、`work_queue.py`、`metrics.py`、`s3_utils.py`、`image_utils.py`、`datatypes.py`、`check.py`、`repeatdetect.py`、`version.py`）各自的一句话职责。
2. 说出七个子包（`prompts/`、`filter/`、`data/`、`train/`、`bench/`、`synth/`、`viewer/`）分别管哪一段事情。
3. 画出模块间的依赖方向草图：`pipeline`（推理）与 `train`（训练）是两个"消费端"，`bench`、`prompts`、`data` 是被双方共享的底层。
4. 把 `pyproject.toml` 里的各个 pip extras 与仓库里的子包对应起来——"装了什么 extras，才有哪部分代码能跑"。

本讲不深入任何一个模块的内部实现（那是第 2~7 单元的事），只建立一张**全局代码地图**。以后读到任何一篇讲义，你都能立刻定位"这个文件在地图的哪个位置、它的上下游是谁"。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲只需要几个很轻的 Python 概念，用通俗语言过一遍：

- **模块（module）与包（package）**：一个 `.py` 文件就是一个模块；一个含 `__init__.py` 的目录就是一个包。`olmocr/work_queue.py` 对应模块 `olmocr.work_queue`；`olmocr/prompts/` 目录对应包 `olmocr.prompts`。
- **`__init__.py` 的作用**：包被 `import` 时最先执行的文件，通常用来"转发"子模块里的重要名字。例如 `from olmocr.prompts import PageResponse` 能直接用，是因为 `prompts/__init__.py` 里替你 `from .prompts import PageResponse` 了。
- **抽象基类（abc）**：用 `@abc.abstractmethod` 声明"子类必须实现这些方法"的父类。`work_queue.py` 的 `Backend` 就是它——定义了"一个存储后端该会做什么"，具体怎么做交给 `LocalBackend` 和 `S3Backend`。本讲只需要知道这个角色分工。
- **pip extras**：第 u1-l2 讲已经装过 `pip install olmocr`。`pyproject.toml` 里 `[project.optional-dependencies]` 定义的 `gpu`、`bench`、`train` 等分组就是 extras——不装它们，`olmocr` 主体仍能 import，只是对应功能的代码在运行时会因缺依赖而失败。
- **依赖方向**：如果 A 文件里出现 `from olmocr.B import ...`，就画一条边 A → B，读作"A 依赖 B"。一个健康的代码库里这些箭头应该大体单向、不绕圈。本讲教你用这条规则亲自"测量"出 olmocr 的架构。

承接前面三讲：u1-l1 讲了 olmocr "是什么"（VLM 驱动的 PDF→文本工具箱）；u1-l2 讲了 "怎么装"（系统依赖 + pip extras 分层）；u1-l3 讲了 "怎么跑出第一个结果"（workspace 五大产物、`olmocr` 命令经 `cli_main()` 进入异步 `main()`）。本讲回答第四个问题：**"代码长什么样、怎么分区"**。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲涉及的文件（按重要程度排序）：

| 文件 | 在本讲中的角色 |
|---|---|
| `pyproject.toml` | 入口注册与 extras 划分，模块地图的"官方索引" |
| `olmocr/pipeline.py` | 全仓库最大的文件（1500+ 行），核心流水线 + CLI 入口 |
| `olmocr/work_queue.py` | 工作队列抽象（`WorkItem`/`Backend`/`WorkQueue`） |
| `olmocr/prompts/prompts.py`、`olmocr/prompts/__init__.py` | 提示词体系与 `PageResponse` 数据契约 |
| 其余顶层文件与子包 | 逐个"点名"，只看职责不看实现 |

仓库根目录还有 `tests/`（pytest 测试）、`scripts/`（发布等辅助脚本，不随包分发）、`docs/`、`Makefile`、`Dockerfile`、`Dockerfile.with-model`、`CHANGELOG.md` 等，本讲不展开，后面单元用到再讲。

`olmocr/` 包的整体形状（只列目录与 `.py`，省略包内资源文件）：

```text
olmocr/
├── __init__.py            # 只导出 VERSION
├── version.py             # 版本号
├── pipeline.py            # ★ 核心流水线 + CLI 入口
├── work_queue.py          # ★ 工作队列（本地/S3 双后端）
├── metrics.py             # 运行时指标
├── s3_utils.py            # S3/GCS/WEKA 工具函数
├── image_utils.py         # 图片→PDF 转换与格式探测
├── datatypes.py           # PdfOutput 数据类（历史遗留，包内无人引用）
├── check.py               # 环境自检（u1-l2 已精读）
├── repeatdetect.py        # 重复 n-gram 检测器
├── prompts/               # 提示词与锚文本
├── filter/                # PDF 过滤（语言/垃圾内容）
├── data/                  # 渲染与训练数据准备脚本
├── train/                 # SFT/GRPO 训练
```

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 顶层模块清单梳理：olmocr/ 根目录的单文件模块

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

打开任何一个陌生 Python 项目，最有效的第一步不是从 `main` 开始读，而是先**清点根目录的顶层模块**——它们往往是一个项目的"公共名词表"（数据结构、工具函数），而大文件则是"动词表"（流程编排）。olmocr 的根目录有 9 个 `.py` 文件，其中两个带 ★ 的是重头戏：

- `pipeline.py`：整个项目的主流程。你在 u1-l3 敲的 `olmocr` 命令就落在它的 `cli_main()`。
- `work_queue.py`：把"待处理 PDF 列表"变成一个可断点续跑、可多机协同的队列。
- 其余 7 个都是被前者引用的工具/数据模块。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

浏览顶层模块的方法论（本节实践会照此执行）：

1. `ls olmocr/*.py` 拿到清单。
2. 对每个文件只看两样东西：模块级 docstring/常量、顶层 `class` / `def` 的名字。
3. 用一句话回答："如果删掉这个文件，哪类功能会坏？"
4. 对照 `pyproject.toml` 的 `[project.scripts]`，确认命令行入口指向哪个模块。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：不看讲义，说出 `olmocr` 命令从敲下回车到进入异步主流程，依次经过哪两个函数、在哪个文件？

> **答案**：`olmocr/pipeline.py` 中的 `cli_main()`（L1526，由 `pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]` 注册）→ `asyncio.run()` 调用 → `main()`（L1199）。

**练习 2**：`work_queue.py` 里 `Backend`、`LocalBackend`、`S3Backend` 三者的关系是什么？为什么要把 `Backend` 设计成抽象基类？

> **答案**：`Backend` 是抽象基类（L38），用 `@abc.abstractmethod` 规定 8 个存储原语；`LocalBackend`（L238）用本地文件实现，`S3Backend`（L392）用 S3 对象实现。抽象的目的是让上层 `WorkQueue`（L82）完全不关心存储介质——同一套断点续跑逻辑既能在笔记本本地跑，也能在多机 S3 协同跑。

**练习 3**：如果你要在 Python 里打印当前安装的 olmocr 版本号，应该 import 哪个模块、读哪个变量？

> **答案**：`from olmocr.version import VERSION`（或 `import olmocr; olmocr.VERSION`，因为 `olmocr/__init__.py` 第 1 行把它转发出来了；定义在 [olmocr/version.py:11](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/version.py#L11)）。

### 4.2 子包职责速查表：七个子包各管一段

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

顶层文件是"名词表"，子包则是按**生命周期阶段**划分的"车间"：提示词怎么写（prompts）、输入要不要丢弃（filter）、页面怎么变成图片（data）、模型怎么训练（train）、效果怎么评（bench）、训练数据怎么造（synth）、结果怎么人工抽查（viewer）。理解子包 = 理解 olmOCR 这个项目的业务闭环：

```text
真实 PDF ──(pipeline 主流水线，用 prompts/data/filter)──> Markdown/Dolma
                                        │
     synth 合成数据 + data 里的 GPT-4o silver 数据
                                        │
                                        ▼
                            train（SFT + GRPO，奖励来自 bench）
                                        │
                                        ▼
                            bench 评测 ──> viewer 人工抽查
```

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

速查一个子包的三步法：

1. 看子包 `__init__.py` 转发了哪些名字——那是作者认定的"对外接口"。
2. 看 `ls` 里文件名的动词前缀（`build_`/`prepare_`/`run_`/`mine_`）——它们大多是可直接运行的脚本。
3. 问自己：这个包服务的是**推理时**、**训练前**还是**训练后**？

### 4.3 模块间依赖草图：谁 import 谁

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

架构不是画出来的，是 **import 出来的**。把每个文件里的 `from olmocr.X import ...` 收集起来，就得到一张真实的依赖图。olmocr 的依赖图呈清晰的"沙漏形"：

- **上层（消费端）**：`pipeline.py`（推理）与 `train/`（训练）——两个各自完整的程序；
- **中层（领域层）**：`prompts/`、`data/`、`filter/`、`bench/`——推理和训练都要用的共享能力；
- **底座（基础设施）**：`s3_utils.py`、`work_queue.py`、`metrics.py`、`image_utils.py` 等工具文件。

关键结论（也是本讲规格要求的学习目标）：**`pipeline`、`work_queue`、`train`、`bench` 四者中，`pipeline` 和 `train` 是平级的两个入口；`work_queue` 只服务于 `pipeline`（及其多机扩展）；`bench` 是 `train`（GRPO 奖励）与 `synth`（质检）共同依赖的下游裁判。**

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

推导依赖草图的伪代码：

```text
对 olmocr/ 下每个 .py 文件 F：
    抽取 F 中所有 "from olmocr.X..." 与 "import olmocr.X..." 行
    对每个 X 画边 F → X
忽略指向自身的边，得到边集 E

观察 E：
    1. 入度最高的节点 = 公共底座（预期：data.renderpdf、s3_utils、prompts）
    2. 出度最高的节点 = 总装配厂（预期：pipeline.py）
    3. 若出现环 = 值得警惕的设计（预期：没有）
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

四条最有代表性的"依赖边"，每条都给出了铁证：

**边 1：pipeline → 几乎全世界。** [olmocr/pipeline.py:32-52](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L32-L52) 的 import 块一口气引了 `check`、`data.renderpdf`、`filter.filter`、`image_utils`、`metrics`、`prompts`、`prompts.anchor`、`s3_utils`、`train.front_matter`、`version`、`work_queue` 共 11 个内部模块——它是唯一"认识所有车间"的总装配厂：


**边 3：train → bench（olmOCR-2 的灵魂边）。** [olmocr/train/grpo_train.py:34-38](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/train/grpo_train.py#L34-L38)：

训练代码 import 评测代码，正是"把 olmOCR-Bench 单元测试当作 GRPO 奖励函数"这一核心创新在依赖图上的投影（u6-l3 精读）。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `olmocr/` 根目录 9 个 `.py` 是"名词表"：`pipeline.py` 是总装配厂与 CLI 入口，`work_queue.py` 提供可断点续跑的队列抽象（`Backend` + 本地/S3 双实现），其余是 metrics/s3/image/check/version 等工具与 `datatypes.py` 这个已无人引用的历史遗留。
- 七个子包按生命周期分工：`prompts`（提示词与输出契约）、`filter`（输入筛选）、`data`（渲染与数据准备）、`train`（SFT/GRPO）、`bench`（单元测试式评测）、`synth`（合成数据）、`viewer`（人工抽查）。
- 依赖图是"沙漏形"：`pipeline` 与 `train` 是平级消费端，`data.renderpdf`/`s3_utils`/`prompts`/`filter` 是被反复复用的腰部底座；`train/grpo_train → bench.tests` 这条"灵魂边"是 olmOCR-2 奖励机制的源码投影。
- `pyproject.toml` 的 extras（`gpu`/`bench`/`train`…）与子包一一对应：轻量安装可 import `prompts`/`work_queue`，但 `train`/`bench` 需要各自的 extras——地图即安装清单。
- 包名 ≠ 分层：`train/front_matter.py` 被推理流水线反向复用，读代码时要以 import 边而非目录名判断真实角色。

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
